chunks: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear the khazz coat for fifty dinars and the khazz shawl for fifty dinars.

key_terms.الجُبَّة: Jubba — a long outer coat or robe, common formal wear in early Islamic civilization
key_terms.الخَزّ: Khazz — a prestigious fabric woven from silk mixed with wool or other fibers; its permissibility was debated and the Imams' use of it was cited as evidence of its lawfulness
key_terms.الدِّينَار: Dinar — a gold coin used as currency in the Islamic world
key_terms.المِطْرَف: Mitrafa — a square shawl or wrap, typically of fine cloth, often worn over the shoulders

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Zayn al-Abidin wear khazz garments?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) narrates that his ancestor Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) used to wear garments made of khazz — a prestigious silk-mixed fabric — valued at fifty dinars each. This hadith is cited in the chapter on wearing khazz to establish that such garments were worn by the Imams of Ahlulbayt, indicating their permissibility. The mention of fifty dinars each emphasizes these were fine, high-quality garments, not a sign of worldly excess but rather of dignified appearance befitting an Imam.
